description: Search for PATTERNS in each FILE.
GNU grep is the default on Linux, WSL, Git for Windows and NetBSD.

option.name: --after-context
tip: Print NUM lines of trailing context after matching lines.
Places a line containing -- between contiguous groups of matches.

option.name: --basic-regexp
tip: PATTERNS are basic regular expressions.

option.name: --before-context
tip: Print NUM lines of leading context before matching lines.
Places a line containing -- between contiguous groups of matches.

option.name: --binary
tip: Do not strip CR characters at EOL (MSDOS/Windows).
This option has no effect on other platforms.

option.name: --binary-files
tip: Assume that binary files are TYPE.
TYPE is 'binary', 'text', or 'without-match'.
Possible values: binary, text, without-match.

option.name: --byte-offset
tip: Print the byte offset with output lines.
With -o, print the offset of the matching part itself.

option.name: --colour
tip: Use markers to highlight the matching strings.
WHEN is 'always', 'never', or 'auto'.
Possible values: always, never, auto.
The value must be attached with =.

option.name: --context
tip: Print NUM lines of output context.
The obsolete -NUM form is the same as -C NUM.

option.name: --count
tip: Print only a count of selected lines per FILE.
With -v, count non-matching lines.

option.name: --dereference-recursive
tip: Like --directories=recurse, but follow all symbolic links.

option.name: --devices
tip: How to handle devices, FIFOs and sockets.
ACTION is 'read' or 'skip'.
Possible values: read, skip.

option.name: --directories
tip: How to handle directories.
ACTION is 'read', 'recurse', or 'skip'.
Possible values: read, recurse, skip.

option.name: --exclude
tip: Skip files that match GLOB.
May be given multiple times.

option.name: --exclude-dir
tip: Skip directories that match GLOB.
May be given multiple times.

option.name: --exclude-from
tip: Skip files that match any file pattern from FILE.
May be given multiple times.

option.name: --extended-regexp
tip: PATTERNS are extended regular expressions.

option.name: --file
tip: Take PATTERNS from FILE.
May be given multiple times.

option.name: --files-with-matches
tip: Print only names of FILEs with selected lines.
The scanning of each file stops on the first match.

option.name: --files-without-match
tip: Print only names of FILEs with no selected lines.
The scanning of each file stops on the first match.

option.name: --fixed-strings
tip: PATTERNS are strings.

option.name: --group-separator
tip: Print SEP on the line between matches with context.
The default is --.

option.name: --help
tip: Display this help text and exit.

option.name: --ignore-case
tip: Ignore case distinctions in patterns and data.

option.name: --include
tip: Search only files that match GLOB (a file pattern).
May be given multiple times.

option.name: --initial-tab
tip: Make tabs line up (if needed).
Useful with options that prefix their output to the content, such as -H, -n and -b.

option.name: --invert-match
tip: Select non-matching lines.

option.name: --label
tip: Use LABEL as the standard input file name prefix.
Useful for tools like zgrep.

option.name: --line-buffered
tip: Flush output on every line.
This can cause a performance penalty.

option.name: --line-number
tip: Print line number with output lines.

option.name: --line-regexp
tip: Match only whole lines.

option.name: --max-count
tip: Stop after NUM selected lines.
With -c, do not output a count greater than NUM.
With -v, stop after NUM non-matching lines.

option.name: --no-filename
tip: Suppress the file name prefix on output.
This is the default when there is only one file (or only standard input) to search.

option.name: --no-group-separator
tip: Do not print a separator for matches with context.

option.name: --no-ignore-case
tip: Do not ignore case distinctions (default).
Useful for cancelling -i in a script.

option.name: --no-messages
tip: Suppress error messages about nonexistent or unreadable files.

option.name: --null
tip: Print a 0 byte after FILE name.

option.name: --null-data
tip: A data line ends in 0 byte, not newline.

option.name: --only-matching
tip: Show only nonempty parts of lines that match.
Each such part is printed on a separate output line.

option.name: --perl-regexp
tip: PATTERNS are Perl regular expressions.
Experimental when combined with -z; grep -P may warn of unimplemented features.

option.name: --recursive
tip: Like --directories=recurse.
Follow symbolic links only if they are on the command line.

option.name: --regexp
tip: Use PATTERNS for matching.
May be given multiple times.

option.name: --silent
tip: Suppress all normal output.
Exit immediately with zero status if any match is found, even if an error was detected.

option.name: --text
tip: Equivalent to --binary-files=text.

option.name: --version
tip: Display version information and exit.

option.name: --with-filename
tip: Print file name with output lines.
This is the default when there is more than one file to search.

option.name: --word-regexp
tip: Match only whole words.
Word-constituent characters are letters, digits and the underscore.
This option has no effect if -x is also specified.

option.name: -I
tip: Equivalent to --binary-files=without-match.
